answers.risk_areas: Move Mobs With Pathfinding (Epic 4) - highest technical risk due to pathfinding algorithms, obstacle detection, path validation. Execute Mob Actions (Epic 2) - medium risk with coordination logic and targeting strategies. Deploy Mobs From Templates (Epic 3) - medium risk with template persistence/storage. Organize Minions Into Mobs (Epic 1) - lower risk, foundational grouping logic.
answers.early_value_areas: Organize Minions Into Mobs (Epic 1) - highest early value, foundational and enables all other epics, represents minimal viable product. Execute Mob Actions (Epic 2) - high early value, core functionality users expect. Deploy Mobs From Templates (Epic 3) - medium value, efficiency improvement but not essential initially. Move Mobs With Pathfinding (Epic 4) - lower early value, enhancement feature that can come later.
answers.complexity_value_ratio: Move Mobs With Pathfinding (Epic 4) - highest complexity/value ratio, complex algorithms (A-star, obstacle avoidance) for enhancement feature. Deploy Mobs From Templates (Epic 3) - medium complexity/value, requires persistence infrastructure for efficiency gains. Execute Mob Actions (Epic 2) - lower complexity/value, moderate complexity for high-value core functionality. Organize Minions Into Mobs (Epic 1) - lowest complexity/value, simpler implementation for foundational value.
answers.thin_slices_end_to_end: Yes - each increment should include complete user journeys (e.g., form mob -> execute action -> see result) to deliver value early and enable feedback.
answers.reusable_components: Core domain concepts reused across all epics: Mob, MinionMember, BoardToken. Strategy patterns reused in Epics 2 and 4: TargetingStrategy (Epic 2), PathfindingStrategy (Epic 4) - similar pattern. Foundry VTT integration reused across all epics: FoundryScene, FoundryActor, BoardToken interactions.
answers.project_constraints: None identified at this time. No delivery timeline/deadlines, resource constraints, Foundry VTT version compatibility requirements, or integration dependencies specified.
answers.user_groups_phased_rollout: GameMaster is the only user type identified. No multiple user groups requiring phased rollout. Note: If there are different GM experience levels (beginner vs advanced), that could affect prioritization.
